A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C.9 are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original forecasting accuracy and inference-time experiments, tokenizer ablations, robustness tests, and representation analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds benchmark evaluations, an input-length control, and further conditional-decoding experiments.

M1.justification: The BPE tokenizer, T5 training objective, and default first-order decoder are retained. Appendix C.3 adds second- and third-order decoding variants and a procedure that quantizes continuous patch-model forecasts before conditional decoding. These are localized procedural extensions.

E1.justification: v4 retains Chronos training and the five original evaluation datasets, adding Solar photovoltaic forecasting and 37 selected Fev-bench datasets spanning cloud, economy, energy, mobility, and retail (Appendix B, Table 8). This substantially broadens evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Time-MoE base and large models and LightGTS to the existing patch-based Chronos, MOMENT, and Moirai comparison. The sample-based Chronos and non-foundation comparator sets elsewhere are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a controlled comparison using 384 time-series samples for both Chronos and motif models, alongside the retained 128-token comparison. New protocols cover Fev-bench sequence filtering and aggregation, higher-order decoding, and post-processing patch-model forecasts. The original training budgets and forecast horizon remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether longer inputs explain forecasting gains (Table 15), whether conditioning on additional previous samples helps (Table 17), and whether conditional decoding benefits continuous-output patch models (Table 18). The noise, non-stationarity, transient, and embedding analyses already appeared in v3.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same six-seed, five-dataset MSE standard deviations for selected small models (v3 Table 9; v4 Table 10). The stated training seed, timing warm-up and measurement counts, and timing uncertainty reporting are also unchanged.

E6.justification: The original five-dataset results are retained, while v4 adds benchmark, baseline, and controlled-analysis results. Section 5.1 changes reported average MSE reduction and acceleration from 36.1% and 19.90× to 39.8% and 23.14× under expanded coverage, not identical settings. The new Solar result is internally inconsistent: Tables 2–3 report 0.439 without conditional decoding, whereas Table 12 reports a best value of 0.493.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 refines tokenization complexity from O(n) to O(|Ψ|·n), explicitly accounting for vocabulary size. The quantization-error bounds and analytical first-order conditional-decoding derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction raise the claimed forecasting improvement from 36% to 40%, efficiency boost from 1990% to 2314%, and conditional-decoding improvement from up to 44% to 48%. These update quantitative claims under broader evaluation; the three central contributions and conclusion remain substantively stable.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly interprets target-data conditional decoding as domain adaptation (Section 5.3), attributes matched-input gains to motif expressiveness (Appendix C.2), and discusses marginal higher-order benefits versus parameter growth (Appendix C.3). Existing robustness interpretations and limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v4 documents the Fev-bench dataset selection and filtering, specifies vocabulary-creation order for motif iteration in Algorithm 2, and reports that estimating conditional-decoding distributions generally takes under 10 seconds. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations for Fev-bench, Time-MoE, and LightGTS. Related work now discusses predefined multiple patch lengths and dominant-frequency-based patch selection, positioning motif tokenization against their limitations in capturing arbitrary-length patterns within a sequence.

P1.justification: Changes include local copyediting, more consistent sample-based terminology, expanded explanations, and updated affiliation and publication-header text. The main section structure and appendices A–C.9 remain, with limited reordering within Appendix C.2.

P2.justification: v4 expands Tables 2, 3, and 12, adds Tables 8, 15, 17, and 18, and adds panels to Figures 9 and 10. Table 3 gains comparator columns, while appendix body text increases from approximately 9 to 10 points, producing widespread reflow and relocation of retained material.

improvement.justification: The equal-input-length control in Table 15 addresses an important ambiguity in v3 about whether gains arose from longer raw contexts. Broader domain coverage, additional contemporary baselines, and the higher-order ablation substantially strengthen the empirical support and design justification. Explicitly identifying target-data decoding as domain adaptation improves interpretation. These gains outweigh the localized new Solar reporting inconsistency between Tables 2–3 and Table 12.
